question: Should Reef core permanently own and support the Node/PostgreSQL relay, container image, and Helm compatibility contract alongside Cloudflare?
rationale: The existing agreed architecture owns a Cloudflare relay, while this PR adds a second persistent backend and deployment platform whose release, migration, security, and upgrade obligations require explicit long-term sponsorship.

options.title: Keep Cloudflare-Only For Now
options.body: Leave the PR in draft or close it until a maintainer explicitly sponsors the additional platform and its continuing release and upgrade obligations.

options.title: Adopt Both Relay Platforms
options.body: Approve Node/PostgreSQL and Helm as supported Reef surfaces after the proxy boundary is repaired and real cluster install and upgrade proof is attached.

options.title: Externalize Kubernetes Packaging
options.body: Preserve only a narrowly approved shared relay interface in core and maintain the Node/PostgreSQL deployment adapter outside this repository.

recommendation.title: Keep Cloudflare-Only For Now
recommendation.body: Leave the PR in draft or close it until a maintainer explicitly sponsors the additional platform and its continuing release and upgrade obligations.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository design explicitly identifies Peter with the agreed current relay architecture, making him the strongest available owner for this scope decision.
